title: Hemodynamics and mesenteric vEnous marKers in sepsis-associated colonic ischemia: Towards optimized Operative strategy
summary:
In cases of severe infection (sepsis), blood flow to the intestine may be impaired. This can lead to damage to parts of the large intestine, which may need to be surgically removed. It is often difficult for the treating physicians to determine exactly how much of the intestine needs to be removed during surgery.

The study investigates whether certain blood test results can help better assess the condition of the intestine and thus improve treatment.

To this end, blood samples are taken from various blood vessels during surgery. In addition to standard blood tests, blood samples are also collected from an intestinal vein to look for signs of potential bacterial spread from the intestine into the body. The results are then compared with the patients’ disease progression and treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sepsis-3 criteria fullfilled
Patient needs an emergency (partial) colectomy
informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
withdraw of informed consent
Inability to collect blood from the relevant mesenteric vein.
primary colonic diseases (e.g. Colitis ulcerosa, M. crohn)
Acute Mesenteric ischemia with occlusion of Truncus coeliacus, superior/inferior mesenteric arterie
